statements.says: For a bilateral contract, the other party's nonperformance permits a claim for performance or rescission after notice to the debtor, with damages where appropriate.
An automatic-rescission clause does not dispense with notice, which is determined by custom when the contracting parties have not specified it.
Compensation is not due until the debtor has been put on notice, unless a provision states otherwise.
The debtor may be put on notice by a warning or an act equivalent to a warning.
Notice may be given by post in the manner prescribed by the Civil Code.
An agreement may make the debtor automatically in default when the obligation falls due, without any further procedure.
Notice is unnecessary in the cases listed in this article.
Notice is unnecessary when the debtor's act makes performance impossible or useless.
Notice is unnecessary when the obligation is compensation arising from a harmful act.
Notice is unnecessary for returning a thing the debtor knows is stolen or received without entitlement while knowing that fact.
Notice is unnecessary when the debtor declares in writing an intention not to perform the obligation.
Articles 176 to 181 also apply to compensation fixed in the contract or a subsequent agreement.

priorSteps.requiredWhen: Before claiming performance or rescission of a bilateral contract following the other party's nonperformance under article 119 paragraph 1; an automatic-rescission clause alone does not dispense with notice under article 120 paragraph 2.
notRequiredWhen: An agreement makes the debtor automatically in default when the obligation falls due, without further procedure; its interaction with article 120 paragraph 2 remains an open point.
The debtor's act makes performance impossible or useless.
The obligation is compensation arising from a harmful act.
The obligation is returning a thing the debtor knows is stolen.
The obligation is returning a thing received without entitlement while the debtor knew that fact.
The debtor declares in writing an intention not to perform.

priorSteps.requiredWhen: Before compensation becomes due, including compensation fixed by agreement; article 179 paragraph 1 does not expressly require notice before filing the claim.
notRequiredWhen: A contrary provision dispenses with notice.
An agreement makes the debtor automatically in default when the obligation falls due, without further procedure.
The debtor's act makes performance impossible or useless.
The obligation is compensation arising from a harmful act.
The obligation is returning a thing the debtor knows is stolen.
The obligation is returning a thing received without entitlement while the debtor knew that fact.
The debtor declares in writing an intention not to perform.
priorSteps.sanctionIfMissing: Compensation is not due before notice, subject to the applicable exceptions; no procedural filing sanction is stated.

openPoints.question: What procedural consequence follows when notice required by article 119 or article 120 is missing?
readings: Article 119 expressly places notice before the demand for performance or rescission, and article 120 preserves notice despite an automatic-rescission clause.
The supplied texts do not select inadmissibility, rejection on the merits, postponement, or an opportunity to cure as the procedural consequence.

openPoints.question: Must notice for compensation precede filing, and can judicial service or later notice satisfy the requirement?
readings: Article 179 expressly conditions entitlement to compensation on notice, without expressly prescribing notice before filing.
A claim for performance or rescission accompanied by damages also engages article 119's prior-notice wording.
Article 180 permits an equivalent to a warning, but the supplied texts do not establish whether service of a claim qualifies or whether notice during proceedings cures an earlier omission.

openPoints.question: Does an article 180 automatic-default agreement satisfy the notice retained by article 120?
readings: Article 180 can be read as supplying deemed notice at maturity, satisfying the notice requirement without a separate act.

Article 120 specifically preserves notice for automatic rescission; the supplied texts do not expressly address whether its requirement is satisfied by the separate agreement contemplated by article 180.

openPoints.question: Which notice means, contents and service events are sufficient?
readings: Article 180 permits a warning, an equivalent act, and postal notice complying with the Code.
The supplied text neither requires a bailiff exclusively nor establishes that registered post with acknowledgement of receipt automatically satisfies every requirement.
The choice other cannot automatically be rejected because equivalent acts are permitted, but qualifying acts are not defined.
The texts do not determine whether dispatch, delivery or receipt is decisive, or whether a non-conciliation record constitutes an equivalent warning.

openPoints.question: Does article 120 paragraph 2 prescribe a notice period?
readings: It refers to determination by the parties or, failing that, custom, without supplying a numerical period.
The wording does not expressly identify whether that determination concerns timing, notice arrangements, or both; no minimum waiting period or counting rule can be derived.

openPoints.question: Can the available slots establish every prerequisite and exemption?
readings: The slots do not establish the relief sought, bilateral contractual nonperformance, an automatic-default agreement, or the circumstances listed in article 181.
Consequently, notice_served being no does not by itself establish a breach of the notice requirement, and notice_served being yes does not establish compliance with unspecified formal requirements.
The supplied paragraphs establish no formal-notice variation based on the remaining employment, public-body, property-registration, residence or contract-date slots.
